name: abyss
avoid: Никакой выдумки, поданной как факт. Не смаковать жестокость ради шока. Не выдавать версии за доказанное.
script_extra:
English-language documentary about one engineering or structural failure.

Work from what an official inquiry established. Name the structure, the year, the operator, the engineers, the report. If a fact is disputed, say it is disputed.

Open on the ordinary day and the ordinary people, named and specific. Build the chain of small decisions that made the outcome inevitable — each one reasonable on its own at the time. Then the failure itself, minute by minute, in plain language a non-engineer follows. Then the aftermath: what the inquiry found, what was changed in the codes, and what was not.

NEVER speculate about what victims experienced. Never invent dialogue or interior thoughts. Never linger on suffering for effect. The restraint is the tone.

VISUAL CUES: directing notes in SQUARE BRACKETS — the structure, the era, where archive or diagrams belong. Stripped before the voice-over.
topic_formula:
English-language documentary reconstructions of ENGINEERING AND STRUCTURAL FAILURES. This is a SUB-NICHE, deliberately narrower than 'disasters in general': dam breaks, bridge and building collapses, tunnel and mine failures, industrial plant accidents, crowd-crush at structures. Not aviation, not shipwrecks, not natural disasters — those are the crowded centre of the niche where 1.4M-subscriber channels already sit.

MEASURED on the reference niche (Fascinating Horror: 1.44M subs, median 349,559 views, 11 min; Plainly Difficult: 1.1M subs, median 238,032, 13 min). Even their weakest videos clear 37,000. Both publish every 6 days.

WHY THIS SUB-NICHE: the material is finite for any one channel but enormous in total, every case has an official inquiry report to work from (so the facts are checkable, not invented), and the visuals are structures and archive — no living faces required.

A title works when it names the STRUCTURE and the SCALE of what happened: 'The Dam That Failed Twice', 'The Bridge That Fell While Being Inspected'. It fails when it is a generic mystery hook with no named object.

HARD RULE: real people died in these events. Never speculate about what victims felt, never invent dialogue, never use a death toll as a hook in the title. State what the inquiry established and stop there. The restraint is the tone of this niche, and audiences punish channels that break it.
used_topics: Footage of the Dyatlov Pass incident
Mysterious disappearances at national parks
The Bridge That Collapsed Twice During Construction
The Hotel Walkways That Collapsed From a Simple Sketch Revision
The Mine Shaft That Collapsed During Routine Maintenance
The Stadium Roof That Collapsed Under Winter Snow
The Dam That Failed Due To A Forgotten Drainage Pipe
The Tunnel That Flooded During Concrete Pouring
The Chemical Plant That Exploded During A Routine Pressure Test
The Grain Elevator That Collapsed Due To Undetected Soil Instability
The Power Station That Collapsed During The Cooling Tower Construction

notes: True crime. Конвейерная модель ниши: Abyssal Detective 475k, 56 мин, раз в 3 дня, медиана 253k. Решает ШИРОТА предмета: широкие визуальные темы x6-11, узкие бытовые x0.17.

name: The Home Vault
avoid: Не пугать ради кликов. Без медицинских утверждений без источника. Не советовать опасные смеси бытовой химии.
script_extra:
This is a practical home-care channel: professional cleaning and
repair methods an ordinary person can do without buying products or calling a
specialist.

FORMAT (measured in this exact niche, not assumed):
- ONE video = ONE specific task, named in the title as "How to <task>".
  On a 2.3M-subscriber channel in this niche, single-task videos of 9-14
  minutes beat the channel median 7-28x, while 23-minute "full episodes"
  covering several topics managed only 3-5x — same channel, same audience.
- Keep to 10-14 minutes. Every successful channel here sits at 6-9 minutes
  median. Do not pad to fill time; stop when the task is done.

Every video must leave the viewer able to DO the thing today. Give exact
quantities, times and temperatures — "a cup of white vinegar, left forty
minutes", not "some vinegar for a while".

Always explain WHY the method works — the chemistry or the mechanics. That is
what separates this from a list of tips and makes it trustworthy.

Where a commercial product is criticised, be specific and fair: name the
actual ingredient and the actual problem with it. No blanket scare claims.

Always state the limits: what must never be mixed, which surfaces the method
damages, when a professional genuinely is needed.

Tone: a competent friend who has done this a hundred times. Warm, calm, never
condescending, never salesy.
topic_formula:
Frugal home fixes: professional-grade results with cheap materials
and no specialist.

MEASURED on a 302k-subscriber channel in exactly this niche, median 96k views.
Same channel, same audience, 250x spread between best and worst:

  WON x4-20:
    "KILL EVERY Mosquito The AMISH Way. SAFE For Honey Bees & Pets"  1.9M
    "The $4 Amish Fix for a Deadly Hot House (Save $3000 This Summer)"  1.65M
    "Cool a Room for $7 FOREVER... No Electricity, No AC"  737k
    "Stop Buying Laundry Detergent - This Cheap $6 Recipe (Lasts a Year)"  589k
    "The $3 Trick That Makes Any Metal Rust-Proof Forever... They Never
     Taught You This"  542k
    "The Ancient Powder That Kills Any Bug... And Why Pest Control
     Companies Hate It"  610k

  LOST x0.03-0.12:
    "5 Things to NEVER Pour Down Your Kitchen Drain"  7.6k
    "15 Plumbing SECRETS to Save You From Ever Calling a Plumber"  6.9k
    "AVOID These 7 Dethatching Mistakes That RUIN Your Lawn"  3.4k
    "3 GENIUS New Pallet Ideas Everyone's Copying this SUMMER"  11k

THE THREE ELEMENTS EVERY WINNING TOPIC HAS. Aim for all three:

  1. A SPECIFIC PRICE. "$4", "$7", "$6", "$3", "$20", "$300". Not "cheap",
     not "budget" — an actual number. Often paired with the money saved:
     "(Save $3000 This Summer)".

  2. A PERMANENCE CLAIM. "FOREVER", "Lasts a Year", "50 Years",
     "Rust-Proof Forever". The viewer is buying an end to a recurring
     problem, not a tip.

  3. WITHHELD KNOWLEDGE. "Why Pest Control Companies Hate It", "They Never
     Taught You This", "The Paint Industry Hopes You Never Learn". Someone
     profits from you not knowing — name them.

WHAT KILLS A TOPIC HERE: numbered lists. Every single flop was a list —
"5 Things", "15 Secrets", "7 Mistakes", "3 Ideas". A list promises browsing;
these viewers want ONE solution to ONE expensive problem. Never write a
numbered-list topic for this channel.

ONE problem, ONE cheap fix, one video. The problem must be one people
currently pay money to solve — pest control, cooling, detergent, rust,
plumbing call-outs. That is where the price comparison bites.

name: Pensamiento Estoico - ES
avoid: Никаких приветствий. Не утверждать, что чувствует конкретный человек зрителя — только закономерности. Без лозунгов и самопомощи «выбери себя» — в этой нише такое проваливается в 100 раз.
script_extra:
Spanish-language documentary about a philosopher or a single work.

SHAPE: follow one mind through time. What happened to this person, and what it made them think. Alternate between the life and the idea it produced, so neither runs dry. There is no withheld mystery here — the pull is watching a worldview being forged and what it cost the person who forged it.

NEVER address the viewer's own life. No 'you', no advice, no lessons to apply. This is measured, not taste: on the reference channel the same author scored 199,346 views when the subject was his ordeal and 538 when the subject was the viewer's demons.

Name dates, places, correspondents, book titles and the year of publication out loud — they are the spine of a documentary.

STYLE: calm, unhurried, Castilian Spanish. The tone of someone recounting a life they have studied for years, not selling insight. End where the idea outlives the person.

VISUAL CUES: directing notes in SQUARE BRACKETS — period, location, where archive material belongs. They are stripped before the voice-over.
topic_formula:
Spanish-language long-form documentaries about philosophers, their lives and the ideas those lives produced.

MEASURED on the reference channel (54 videos, median 19,738 views, spread 17x between best and worst):
  WON  330k-166k : why intelligence leads to loneliness (Schopenhauer); the philosopher who reinvented God (Spinoza); the genius who descended into the darkness of the human soul (Dostoyevsky); the book that drove Jung to the edge of the abyss; the warning the world refused to hear (Orwell)
  LOST 1.7k-538  : existentialist philosophy explained; HOW TO BECOME the man Nietzsche admired; HOW TO BUILD a just society (Rousseau); the book that reveals YOUR inner demons (Jung)

The distinguishing variable is exact, and it is NOT the thinker's name: Jung appears in both halves — 199,346 views for 'the book that drove HIM to the abyss' and 538 for 'the book that reveals YOUR demons'. Same author, same length, same format.

A video WINS when the promise is about what happened TO THE THINKER or TO THE WORLD — third person, past tense, a catastrophe or a cost.
A video FAILS when the promise is about what the VIEWER should do or get — 'how to become', 'how to build', 'your demons'. Never write a title in the second person.

Already covered on the reference channel, do NOT repeat: Schopenhauer, Spinoza, Dostoyevsky, Nietzsche, Jung's Red Book, Orwell's 1984, Musashi.

Length is table stakes, not an advantage: the failures run 52-86 minutes too. Target 45 minutes — the short edge of this niche (reference channel runs 43-109 min). Do NOT pad to reach length: a tight 45 beats a padded 70. Win on the promise, not the runtime.
used_topics: El pensador que vio el colapso de la civilización antes que nadie
El hombre que lo perdió todo ante el tirano al que educó
El genio que abandonó la razón tras asomarse al abismo del infinito
